r.정치 구도: A semi-presidential system with a directly elected president and a prime minister chosen by parliament. After protests toppled a pro-Russian government in 2014, it turned toward Europe. Since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, martial law has continued and presidential and parliamentary elections have been postponed. Fighting corruption is a major task tied to the conditions for joining the EU, and there has been controversy over the independence of anti-corruption agencies.

t.why: Its vast black earth lets it export huge amounts of wheat, corn and sunflower oil, earning it the name 'breadbasket of Europe'. When the war blocked Black Sea exports, world grain prices jumped. Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 and has occupied parts of the east and south since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine holds out with weapons and money from the United States and Europe; it became an EU candidate in 2022 and wants to join NATO, but members are divided. Peace talks and the form of security guarantees are major issues for world security.
t.rel: Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, and a full-scale war has raged since 2022. Backed by US and European military and economic aid, it is negotiating to join the EU.
t.korea: The two established relations in 1992. Since the war, Korea has provided humanitarian aid and reconstruction cooperation but has not sent weapons directly. North Korea's dispatch of troops and weapons to Russia has linked this war to security on the Korean Peninsula. Korean construction and energy companies are mentioned for rebuilding projects.
t.know: Ukraine is the world's largest exporter of sunflower oil.
etext: Its dark, fertile black earth makes it a breadbasket that sells lots of wheat, corn and sunflower oil to the world. Its sunflower oil exports are among the largest in the world.
Iron ore and steel were major exports, but they fell sharply when the eastern industrial region became a battlefield. Its outsourced IT developers have kept exporting even during the war.
Grain exports swung wildly as Black Sea routes were blocked and then reopened. Foreign support fills a large part of the budget, and the cost of reconstruction is enormous.
